# MLOps Architect Handbook

## From DevOps Engineer to Senior MLOps / ML Platform Architect

### Volume 1 — Foundations

# Chapter 47 — ML Platform Testing, Verification, and Validation Architecture: Unit Tests, Distributed-System Verification, Data Tests, Model Tests, GPU Compatibility, Performance Qualification, Chaos, DR, Property-Based Testing, and Release Certification

---

# 1. Why Testing an ML Platform Is Fundamentally Different

Traditional application testing often asks:

```text
Does this code produce the expected output?
```

An ML platform must ask much more:

```text
Is the code correct?

Is the distributed state transition correct?

Is the data temporally correct?

Is the model statistically acceptable?

Is the runtime numerically compatible?

Is the deployment recoverable?

Will the system remain correct under retries?

Will it remain correct after worker crashes?

Does performance still meet the SLO?

Can it recover from region failure?
```

This is why testing at architect level is really:

```text
SYSTEM VERIFICATION
```

rather than merely writing unit tests.

---

# 2. Verification vs Validation

Verification asks:

```text
Did we build the system correctly?
```

Validation asks:

```text
Did we build the correct system?
```

Both matter.

---

# 3. Example

Verification:

```text
The feature pipeline computes:
customer_30d_spend
according to its specification.
```

Validation:

```text
customer_30d_spend
actually improves the model
without leakage
and represents the intended business concept.
```

---

# 4. ML Testing Has Multiple Correctness Domains

```text
Code Correctness

API Correctness

State-Machine Correctness

Distributed Correctness

Data Correctness

Temporal Correctness

Model Correctness

Statistical Correctness

Numerical Correctness

Performance Correctness

Recovery Correctness

Security Correctness
```

---

# 5. The Architect Mental Model

```text
REQUIREMENT
    |
    v
INVARIANT
    |
    v
TEST OR PROOF
    |
    v
BUILD ARTIFACT
    |
    v
QUALIFICATION
    |
    v
PROGRESSIVE RELEASE
    |
    v
PRODUCTION EVIDENCE
```

---

# 6. Testing Should Follow Failure Cost

The cheapest place to catch a defect is:

```text
before deployment
```

The most expensive is:

```text
after it corrupts production state
```

---

# 7. Failure-Cost Ladder

```text
Unit Test
   |
   v
Component Test
   |
   v
Integration Test
   |
   v
Staging
   |
   v
Canary
   |
   v
Production Incident
```

Cost generally rises as defects move downward.

---

# 8. The Test Pyramid

Classic form:

```text
          E2E
        /     \
    Integration
   /           \
       Unit
```

Many:

```text
fast deterministic unit tests
```

Fewer:

```text
expensive integration/E2E tests
```

---

# 9. ML Platform Test Pyramid Is Wider

A better mental model:

```text
                  Production Validation
                        /       \
                 Shadow / Canary
                    /           \
             End-to-End / Chaos
                /               \
         Distributed Integration
            /                   \
   Component / Contract / State Tests
          /                     \
      Unit / Property / Static
```

---

# 10. There Is No Single "Test Suite"

A large ML platform may have separate qualification systems for:

```text
control-plane code

data pipelines

model artifacts

serving runtimes

GPU software

infrastructure

security policies
```

---

# 11. Test Strategy Starts With Invariants

Do not begin with:

```text
What tests should we write?
```

Begin with:

```text
What must never become false?
```

---

# 12. Example Scheduler Invariant

```text
A GPU may belong to at most one exclusive allocation.
```

---

# 13. Example Quota Invariant

```text
reserved + consumed <= hard quota
```

unless an explicitly authorized override exists.

---

# 14. Example Registry Invariant

```text
Every production deployment references
an existing immutable model artifact.
```

---

# 15. Example Feature Invariant

```text
Training feature values
must not contain information
that became available after prediction time.
```

---

# 16. Example Deployment Invariant

```text
A deployment cannot receive production traffic
before readiness validation succeeds.
```

---

# 17. Example Checkpoint Invariant

```text
A checkpoint is visible as committed
only after every required shard is durable.
```

---

# 18. Invariants Are More Durable Than Test Cases

Implementation changes.

But:

```text
exclusive GPU ownership
```

remains true.

Design tests around enduring invariants.

---

# 19. Unit Testing

Unit tests verify:

```text
small deterministic logic
```

without real external infrastructure.

---

# 20. Good Unit-Test Targets

```text
quota calculations

placement scoring

retry classification

state transitions

feature transformations

policy decisions
```

---

# 21. Bad Unit-Test Target

Trying to prove:

```text
multi-region failover works
```

using a mocked function call.

That requires higher-level testing.

---

# 22. Pure Functions Are Highly Testable

Example:

```text
score_candidate(job, cluster_state)
```

should ideally be deterministic.

---

# 23. Deterministic Logic

Same input:

```text
X
```

produces same output:

```text
Y
```

This simplifies:

```text
tests

debugging

replay
```

---

# 24. Dependency Injection

External systems should often be abstracted so tests can supply:

```text
fake clock

fake storage

fake quota service

fake event bus
```

---

# 25. Time Is a Dependency

Distributed platforms often contain:

```text
leases

TTL

timeouts

backoff

windows
```

Do not hardwire system wall clock everywhere.

---

# 26. Fake Clock

A test can advance:

```text
t = 10s
-> t = 1h
```

without actually waiting.

---

# 27. Randomness Is a Dependency

Schedulers, sampling, retry jitter may use randomness.

Tests should support:

```text
seeded randomness
```

---

# 28. Property-Based Testing

Instead of manually specifying every input:

```text
generate many valid and invalid combinations
```

and assert invariants.

---

# 29. Example Property

For quota allocator:

```text
for all generated requests:
usage never exceeds hardMax
```

---

# 30. Example Scheduler Property

```text
no two exclusive jobs
are assigned the same GPU
```

across thousands of generated schedules.

---

# 31. Example Retry Property

```text
retry delay is always:

>= minimum
<= maximum
```

for all attempt counts.

---

# 32. Why Property Tests Matter

Distributed/stateful systems have:

```text
huge input spaces
```

that humans will not enumerate manually.

---

# 33. Fuzz Testing

Feed:

```text
unexpected

malformed

extreme
```

inputs into:

```text
APIs

parsers

serializers

protocols
```

---

# 34. API Fuzzing

Useful for:

```text
deeply nested specs

large payloads

invalid enums

Unicode

boundary integers
```

---

# 35. Parser Security

Model or dataset manifests should survive:

```text
malformed metadata
```

without:

```text
crash

resource exhaustion

unsafe interpretation
```

---

# 36. Boundary-Value Testing

Important values include:

```text
0

1

max

max+1

negative

empty

null
```

---

# 37. Quota Boundary Example

Test:

```text
usage = quota - 1

usage = quota

usage = quota + 1
```

---

# 38. Numeric Overflow

Capacity calculations may involve:

```text
billions of tokens

PB storage

large timestamps
```

Test integer bounds.

---

# 39. Unit-Test Anti-Pattern

Testing implementation internals so tightly that harmless refactoring breaks hundreds of tests.

Test:

```text
behavior + invariants
```

more than private structure.

---

# 40. Contract Testing

Contract tests verify:

```text
producer and consumer agree
```

on API/event/data semantics.

---

# 41. API Contract

Includes:

```text
field names

types

required fields

error semantics

version behavior
```

---

# 42. Event Contract

Includes:

```text
event name

schema

ordering assumptions

idempotency key

version
```

---

# 43. Data Contract

Includes:

```text
schema

nullability

ranges

semantics

freshness

ownership
```

---

# 44. Model Artifact Contract

May include:

```text
format

framework/runtime compatibility

tokenizer reference

precision

signature

input/output schema
```

---

# 45. Backward Compatibility Test

Old client:

```text
v1
```

should continue interacting with:

```text
v2 server
```

when compatibility is promised.

---

# 46. Forward Compatibility

New client interacting with old server is harder.

Can use:

```text
feature discovery

optional fields

version negotiation
```

---

# 47. Unknown Fields

A robust API often ignores or preserves unknown fields appropriately.

Test this explicitly.

---

# 48. Enum Evolution

Adding:

```text
NEW_STATUS
```

may break clients that assume all enum values known.

Contract tests should catch such assumptions.

---

# 49. Schema Compatibility

Test:

```text
add optional field

rename field

change type

remove field
```

against compatibility rules.

---

# 50. Golden API Fixtures

Keep representative:

```text
requests

responses

events
```

from previous versions.

---

# 51. Golden Tests

Compare output against known expected artifact.

Useful for:

```text
serialization

compiler IR

policy decisions

feature transformations
```

---

# 52. Golden-Test Risk

Large golden files can hide:

```text
meaningless diffs
```

Review semantic changes, not blindly update snapshots.

---

# 53. Component Testing

Test one real component against:

```text
realistic but isolated dependencies
```

---

# 54. Example Controller Test

Start:

```text
real reconciler
+
temporary DB
+
fake cluster agent
```

---

# 55. State-Machine Testing

Critical platform controllers should have explicit states.

Example:

```text
QUEUED
-> RESERVED
-> STARTING
-> RUNNING
-> SUCCEEDED
```

---

# 56. State Transition Test

Verify:

```text
RUNNING -> QUEUED
```

is either:

```text
forbidden
```

or explicitly modeled.

---

# 57. State-Machine Invariants

Examples:

```text
terminal state does not transition again

resource release happens exactly once logically

generation numbers increase monotonically
```

---

# 58. Transition Matrix

Create:

```text
Current State × Event -> Next State
```

and test all combinations.

---

# 59. Invalid Event Handling

If:

```text
Cancel
```

arrives after:

```text
Succeeded
```

controller should handle predictably.

---

# 60. Duplicate Event Test

Send:

```text
TaskCompleted
TaskCompleted
```

System should remain correct.

---

# 61. Reordered Event Test

Send:

```text
Completion
```

before:

```text
Started
```

if network/event bus may reorder.

---

# 62. Lost Event Test

Drop event entirely.

Reconciliation should eventually converge.

---

# 63. Reconciliation Test

Given:

```text
desired = RUNNING

actual = MISSING
```

controller should recreate/recover according to policy.

---

# 64. Level-Triggered Correctness

Repeated reconciliation:

```text
reconcile()

reconcile()

reconcile()
```

should be safe.

---

# 65. Idempotency Testing

For operation:

```text
CreateDeployment(request_id=123)
```

execute twice.

Expected:

```text
one logical deployment
```

---

# 66. Duplicate Delivery

Message systems often provide:

```text
at-least-once
```

delivery.

Test duplicates deliberately.

---

# 67. Crash-Boundary Testing

The most powerful distributed-system technique:

```text
crash after every important side effect
```

---

# 68. Example

Operation:

```text
1. write DB state
2. create cloud resource
3. publish event
```

Test crash:

```text
before 1

after 1

after 2

after 3
```

---

# 69. Crash After External Side Effect

Dangerous case:

```text
GPU cluster created
```

but process dies before recording success.

Retry must not create another cluster accidentally.

---

# 70. External Idempotency Key

Use stable identity:

```text
job-123-attempt-1
```

for external resource creation.

---

# 71. Unknown Outcome

RPC times out.

Did remote service:

```text
execute
```

or not?

Tests must simulate this ambiguity.

---

# 72. Timeout ≠ Failure

Test:

```text
remote completes successfully
but caller receives timeout
```

Then caller retries.

Correctness must survive.

---

# 73. Network Partition Testing

Simulate:

```text
A can reach B

B cannot reach A
```

or full partition.

---

# 74. Asymmetric Network Failure

Often harder than complete outage.

Test explicitly.

---

# 75. Delayed Messages

Inject:

```text
100 ms

10 sec

5 min
```

latency.

---

# 76. Duplicate Packets/Messages

Useful for protocol verification.

---

# 77. Connection Reset

Kill:

```text
TCP connection
```

during:

```text
artifact upload

streaming inference

checkpoint commit
```

---

# 78. Partial Write

Storage operation may write:

```text
some shards
```

before failure.

Commit protocol must reject incomplete generation.

---

# 79. Torn Workflow

Some tasks completed.

Some did not.

Recovery should recompute only required work.

---

# 80. Lease Expiry Test

Owner pauses beyond TTL.

Another worker acquires lease.

Old worker resumes.

Old worker must be fenced.

---

# 81. Fencing Test

Old generation writes:

```text
epoch=4
```

Current epoch:

```text
5
```

Write must fail.

---

# 82. Split-Brain Test

Force two controllers to believe they are leader.

Verify:

```text
only fenced authority
```

can mutate protected state.

---

# 83. Leadership Transition Test

Kill current leader repeatedly during workload.

State must remain consistent.

---

# 84. Consensus Testing

If using consensus-based component, test:

```text
leader failure

minority partition

majority partition

node rejoin
```

---

# 85. Jepsen-Style Thinking

Ask:

```text
What histories are legal
under concurrent operations and failures?
```

---

# 86. Linearizability Testing

Useful where API promises:

```text
single-copy ordering
```

for critical metadata.

---

# 87. Example Critical Operations

```text
quota reservation

production pointer update

ownership transfer
```

---

# 88. Serializability Testing

Concurrent transactions should behave like:

```text
some serial ordering
```

if serializable semantics are promised.

---

# 89. Write-Skew Test

Two concurrent transactions each observe:

```text
remaining quota = 8
```

and both reserve:

```text
8
```

Test isolation prevents:

```text
16 allocated
```

---

# 90. Compare-and-Swap Test

Verify stale version update fails.

---

# 91. Concurrent Delete/Create

Race:

```text
delete deployment

update deployment
```

System needs defined winner or conflict behavior.

---

# 92. Finalizer Testing

Delete resource while external dependency unavailable.

Finalizer should:

```text
retry cleanup
```

without leaking forever.

---

# 93. Garbage Collection Test

Create:

```text
parent

children

artifacts
```

Delete parent.

Verify correct ownership cleanup.

---

# 94. Orphan Detection Test

Delete metadata but leave external resource.

Reconciler should:

```text
adopt

or delete
```

according to policy.

---

# 95. Integration Testing

Verify multiple real components together.

---

# 96. Example

```text
API
+
DB
+
event bus
+
controller
+
fake execution agent
```

---

# 97. Integration Environment

Should be:

```text
isolated

repeatable

ephemeral
```

where feasible.

---

# 98. Ephemeral Environments

Create test environment per:

```text
PR

branch

test run
```

---

# 99. Environment Reproducibility

Test setup itself should be:

```text
IaC-defined

version-pinned
```

---

# 100. Test Environment Drift

If staging differs substantially from production:

```text
passing tests create false confidence
```

---

# 101. Production-Like Does Not Mean Production-Sized Everywhere

Use:

```text
semantic fidelity
```

for most tests.

Reserve full scale for:

```text
performance

failure

capacity
```

qualification.

---

# 102. Semantic Fidelity

Example:

A 3-node test can still verify:

```text
leader failover semantics
```

even though production has 100 nodes.

---

# 103. Scale Fidelity

Some bugs appear only with:

```text
10k resources

millions of metrics

1000 concurrent workers
```

Those need explicit scale tests.

---

# 104. End-to-End Testing

Verify real user workflow.

Example:

```text
upload dataset
->
define feature
->
train model
->
register
->
deploy
->
predict
```

---

# 105. E2E Tests Are Expensive

They tend to be:

```text
slow

flaky

hard to diagnose
```

Use sparingly.

---

# 106. Critical Journey Tests

Choose a small set covering:

```text
highest-value workflows
```

---

# 107. E2E Result Must Be Diagnosable

On failure, preserve:

```text
trace

logs

resource states

artifact IDs
```

---

# 108. E2E Test Anti-Pattern

One enormous test covers:

```text
everything
```

and fails ambiguously.

Prefer modular journeys.

---

# 109. Distributed-System Test Harness

Provide controls to:

```text
pause process

kill process

delay network

drop messages

advance clock
```

---

# 110. Deterministic Simulation

Where possible, simulate distributed components under:

```text
controlled virtual time
```

---

# 111. Deterministic Scheduler Testing

Replay exact:

```text
job arrival sequence

node state

random seed
```

to reproduce allocation bug.

---

# 112. Model Checking

For small state spaces, formally enumerate:

```text
possible state transitions
```

to prove invariants.

---

# 113. TLA+/Formal Specification Thinking

Especially valuable for:

```text
leader election

quota allocation

ownership transfer

checkpoint commit
```

---

# 114. Formal Methods Are Selective

Do not formally verify every endpoint.

Use where:

```text
failure cost is high

state machine is subtle

concurrency is hard
```

---

# 115. Example Formal Invariant

```text
At most one region may own write epoch E.
```

---

# 116. Example Checkpoint Invariant

```text
Committed manifest references only
durable complete shards.
```

---

# 117. Data Testing

ML correctness begins with:

```text
data
```

---

# 118. Data Test Categories

```text
Schema

Completeness

Validity

Uniqueness

Freshness

Distribution

Referential Integrity

Temporal Correctness
```

---

# 119. Schema Test

Verify:

```text
column names

types

nullability
```

---

# 120. Schema Evolution Test

Check compatibility with:

```text
current consumers
```

before publication.

---

# 121. Completeness

Example:

```text
>99.99% events contain customer_id
```

---

# 122. Validity

Example:

```text
age >= 0

probability ∈ [0,1]
```

---

# 123. Uniqueness

Example:

```text
event_id unique
```

when contract requires.

---

# 124. Referential Integrity

Every:

```text
account_id
```

must map to a valid account where semantics require.

---

# 125. Freshness

Test:

```text
latest_event_time
```

or:

```text
latest_partition
```

within SLO.

---

# 126. Volume Test

Unexpected:

```text
90% drop
```

or:

```text
20× spike
```

may indicate source failure.

---

# 127. Distribution Test

Compare:

```text
mean

quantiles

histogram

category frequencies
```

against expected ranges.

---

# 128. Distribution Tests Should Allow Real Change

Do not reject every legitimate business shift.

Use:

```text
tolerances

seasonality

context
```

---

# 129. Dataset Contract

Defines expected:

```text
semantics

not only schema
```

---

# 130. Semantic Data Test

Column:

```text
approval_timestamp
```

should actually represent:

```text
time approval became known
```

not another timestamp with same type.

---

# 131. Temporal Correctness

Critical for ML.

A feature may have:

```text
event time

processing time

availability time
```

---

# 132. Point-in-Time Correctness Test

For prediction time:

```text
T
```

training row may use only information:

```text
available <= T
```

according to defined semantics.

---

# 133. Leakage Test

Inject future information into source and verify:

```text
PIT join excludes it
```

---

# 134. Availability-Time Test

Event occurred at:

```text
09:00
```

but became available at:

```text
11:00
```

Prediction at:

```text
10:00
```

must not use it if production could not know it.

---

# 135. Late Correction Test

Original value:

```text
v1
```

Later corrected to:

```text
v2
```

Historical reconstruction must follow chosen temporal semantics.

---

# 136. Bitemporal Test

Validate:

```text
effective time

knowledge/transaction time
```

independently.

---

# 137. Backfill Test

Historical recomputation must not accidentally overwrite:

```text
current online serving namespace
```

before safe cutover.

---

# 138. Materialization Test

Offline result and online materialized value should agree under:

```text
same feature definition
```

within defined precision/latency semantics.

---

# 139. Training-Serving Skew Test

Run same canonical feature definition through:

```text
offline engine

online engine
```

and compare.

---

# 140. Skew Taxonomy

Test separately:

```text
transformation skew

null/default skew

temporal skew

version skew

source skew

precision skew
```

---

# 141. Null Semantics

Does:

```text
null
```

mean:

```text
missing

zero

unknown

not applicable
```

?

Test consistently.

---

# 142. Default Value Test

Online serving fallback must match:

```text
training semantics
```

if parity is promised.

---

# 143. Feature Dependency Test

Feature B depends on A.

If A version changes:

```text
does B recompute correctly?
```

---

# 144. Feature DAG Test

Validate:

```text
no cycles

compatible types

deterministic dependencies
```

---

# 145. Streaming Feature Tests

Must include:

```text
out-of-order events

duplicates

late events

watermarks

state expiry
```

---

# 146. Watermark Test

Advance event-time watermark and verify:

```text
window closes
```

at intended point.

---

# 147. Late-Arrival Test

Event arrives:

```text
10 minutes late
```

Test whether:

```text
accepted

revised

dropped
```

according to contract.

---

# 148. Retraction Test

If late correction changes previous aggregate:

```text
old value should be retracted/revised
```

where supported.

---

# 149. Dedupe Test

Send same event:

```text
twice
```

and validate one logical contribution.

---

# 150. Dedupe Window Test

Duplicate arrives after state TTL.

Behavior must match documented semantics.

---

# 151. Streaming Checkpoint Test

Crash processor.

Restore state.

Verify:

```text
no logical gap

bounded duplicate behavior
```

---

# 152. State TTL Test

Advance time beyond TTL and verify:

```text
state removed

new event handled correctly
```

---

# 153. Reprocessing Test

Replay historical log.

Output should be:

```text
deterministic
```

if semantics promise deterministic replay.

---

# 154. Dataset Reproducibility

Training dataset should have immutable identity:

```text
dataset manifest

source snapshots

feature versions
```

---

# 155. Dataset Hash

Can hash:

```text
manifest

partition identities

schema
```

rather than every byte for giant data.

---

# 156. Golden Dataset

Small carefully curated dataset with:

```text
known expected transformations
```

---

# 157. Golden Dataset Purpose

Catch semantic regression in:

```text
features

labels

preprocessing
```

---

# 158. Golden Dataset Should Include Edge Cases

Examples:

```text
missing values

late events

timezone boundaries

duplicate IDs

rare categories
```

---

# 159. Label Testing

Verify:

```text
label definition

label availability time

label leakage

class balance
```

---

# 160. Label Leakage Test

Ensure label-derived fields do not enter feature set before prediction.

---

# 161. Timezone Testing

ML temporal bugs often appear around:

```text
UTC offsets

DST transitions

month boundaries
```

---

# 162. Date Boundary Test

Test:

```text
midnight

month end

year end

leap day
```

where relevant.

---

# 163. Model Testing

Model tests answer:

```text
Is this model acceptable to release?
```

---

# 164. Model Test Categories

```text
Functional

Statistical

Quality

Robustness

Fairness

Safety

Performance

Compatibility
```

---

# 165. Functional Model Test

Can model:

```text
load

accept schema

produce valid output
```

---

# 166. Output Contract Test

Verify:

```text
shape

type

range

required fields
```

---

# 167. NaN/Inf Test

Feed edge inputs.

Ensure outputs do not unexpectedly contain:

```text
NaN

Inf
```

---

# 168. Deterministic Inference Test

If model/runtime promises deterministic inference:

```text
same input
->
same output
```

within defined tolerance.

---

# 169. Statistical Model Test

Evaluate over:

```text
representative dataset
```

---

# 170. Quality Gate

Example:

```text
AUC >= 0.82
```

or:

```text
task success >= 91%
```

---

# 171. Relative Quality Gate

Candidate must satisfy:

```text
candidate >= champion - tolerance
```

---

# 172. Noninferiority Testing

Useful when candidate offers:

```text
lower cost

lower latency
```

while preserving quality within acceptable margin.

---

# 173. Statistical Significance

A tiny quality change may be noise.

Use:

```text
confidence intervals

hypothesis tests
```

where appropriate.

---

# 174. Practical Significance

A statistically significant:

```text
0.01% improvement
```

may have no business value.

---

# 175. Segmented Evaluation

Overall score can hide failures for:

```text
region

device

customer segment

rare class
```

---

# 176. Slice Testing

Define critical slices.

Example:

```text
high-value customers

rare fraud type

long-context prompts
```

---

# 177. Worst-Slice Gate

Candidate may need:

```text
no critical slice regression > X
```

---

# 178. Robustness Test

Perturb:

```text
input noise

missing fields

typos

distribution shift
```

and measure behavior.

---

# 179. Adversarial Testing

For applicable models:

```text
adversarial examples

prompt injection

malformed media
```

---

# 180. Stress Input Test

Extreme but valid:

```text
maximum sequence length

large image

rare category
```

---

# 181. Out-of-Distribution Test

Evaluate behavior on:

```text
known OOD datasets
```

---

# 182. Confidence Calibration

For probabilistic models, verify:

```text
predicted confidence
```

matches empirical correctness reasonably.

---

# 183. Calibration Regression Test

Runtime/model change should not silently alter:

```text
probability calibration
```

if downstream thresholds depend on it.

---

# 184. Threshold Regression

Classifier threshold:

```text
0.7
```

may behave differently after calibration changes.

Test downstream decision metrics.

---

# 185. Ranking Tests

Evaluate:

```text
NDCG

MAP

Recall@K

business ranking metrics
```

---

# 186. Generative Model Evaluation

May include:

```text
task success

factuality

format adherence

safety

human preference
```

---

# 187. LLM Exact-Match Limitation

Many good outputs are semantically equivalent but textually different.

Use task-appropriate metrics.

---

# 188. Structured Output Test

If model must emit JSON:

```text
schema-valid output rate
```

is a first-class reliability metric.

---

# 189. Tool-Calling Test

For agents:

```text
correct tool chosen

arguments valid

unsafe tool not chosen
```

---

# 190. Agent Workflow Test

Test full loop:

```text
plan

tool call

observation

next action

completion
```

---

# 191. Agent Budget Test

Ensure agent respects:

```text
max steps

token budget

cost budget

timeout
```

---

# 192. Agent Idempotency

Retrying tool call after timeout must not:

```text
duplicate irreversible action
```

---

# 193. RAG Testing

Evaluate:

```text
retrieval quality

grounding

citation correctness

answer quality
```

separately.

---

# 194. Retrieval Recall Test

For known questions:

```text
relevant document appears in top-K
```

---

# 195. Reranker Test

Candidate reranker should improve or preserve:

```text
ranking quality
```

within latency budget.

---

# 196. Chunking Regression

Changing chunking parameters can alter retrieval dramatically.

Treat as model/data release.

---

# 197. Embedding Compatibility

New embedding model may make:

```text
old vector index incompatible
```

# 198. Prompt Regression Testing

```text
quality

format

safety

latency

token cost
```

# 199. Prompt Golden Suite

```text
happy path

edge cases

adversarial cases
```

# 200. Prompt Overfitting

Maintain:

```text
holdout evaluation
```

---

# 201. Fairness Testing

Evaluate outcomes across:

```text
relevant protected or business-critical groups
```

when appropriate and lawful.

```text
TPR parity

FPR parity

calibration

selection rates
```

# 203. Fairness Is Not One Metric

# 204. Privacy Testing

```text
restricted features

raw secrets

prohibited fields
```

---

# 205. Data Deletion Test

```text
source

derived data

cache

training snapshots
```

according to policy.

# 206. Security Testing

Includes:

```text
authn

authz

tenant isolation

secret handling

network policy

supply chain
```

---

# 207. Authorization Test

Tenant A attempts to access:

```text
Tenant B model
```

Expected:

```text
denied
```

---

# 208. Negative Security Tests

# 209. Cross-Tenant Cache Test

---

# 210. Token Confusion Test

---

# 211. Secret Exposure Test

Ensure logs/errors do not reveal:

```text
credentials

tokens

private prompts
```

---

# 212. Supply-Chain Verification

```text
signature

SBOM

provenance

builder identity
```

---

# 213. Unsigned Artifact Test


for protected environments.

---

# 214. Dependency Vulnerability Test

Scan:

```text
container

Python packages

system libraries
```

---

# 215. Vulnerability Gate

Policy considers:

```text
severity

exploitability

exposure

waiver
```

---

# 216. Infrastructure Testing

IaC must also be tested.

# 217. Static IaC Test

Check:

```text
syntax

policy

security configuration
```

---

# 218. Plan Review

Inspect:

```text
create

update

destroy
```

before apply.

```text
production database

network

KMS key
```

without approval.

# 220. Ephemeral Infrastructure Test

```text
VPC

cluster

database
```

in disposable environment for critical modules.

# 221. Policy-as-Code Test

```text
ALLOW

DENY

REQUIRE_APPROVAL
```

# 222. Policy Regression Suite

Store representative:

```text
allowed cases

denied cases

edge cases
```

---

# 223. Admission Webhook Test

Test:

```text
timeout

unavailability

malformed request

large request
```

---

# 224. Fail-Open vs Fail-Closed Test

Policy engine outage behavior must match risk.

# 225. Kubernetes Operator Testing

Need:

```text
unit

envtest-like API tests

real cluster tests

upgrade tests
```

---

# 226. CRD Schema Test

Ensure invalid resources rejected early.

# 227. CRD Upgrade Test

Old stored object:

```text
v1alpha1
```

must remain readable after:

```text
v1
```

migration.

---

# 228. Conversion Test

If webhook converts versions:

```text
round-trip conversion
```

should preserve semantics.

# 229. Operator Upgrade Test

Upgrade controller while:

```text
jobs running
```

and verify no duplicate execution.

---

# 230. Mixed-Version Test

During rolling upgrade:

```text
old controller/agent

new controller/agent
```

may coexist.

Test compatibility.

# 231. Kubernetes Scheduler Plugin Test

```text
Filter

Score

Reserve

Permit

Bind
```

behavior independently.

with only:

```text
32
```

available.

```text
no partial execution
```

# 233. Reservation Race Test

Two schedulers try to reserve same GPU group concurrently.

---

# 234. Backfill Test

Short job fits before reservation.

```text
backfill runs
without delaying reservation
```

---

# 235. Duration-Estimate Failure Test

Backfill job overruns.

Test reservation protection behavior.

---

# 236. Preemption Test

High-priority job arrives.

Verify victim choice follows:

```text
policy + topology + checkpoint cost
```

---

# 237. Fairness Test

Generate continuous demand from multiple tenants.

Verify long-window allocations converge toward:

```text
weighted entitlement
```

---

# 238. Starvation Test

Ensure:

```text
eligible job
```

eventually gets service under intended policy.

---

# 239. Priority-Abuse Test

Unauthorized tenant requests:

```text
P0
```

Admission must reject/downgrade.

---

# 240. Quota Borrowing Test

Tenant exceeds soft share using spare capacity.

When lender returns:

```text
borrowed workload reclaimed
```

correctly.

---

# 241. Multi-Region Scheduler Test

Lose global control plane.

Regional schedulers should continue within:

```text
local authority
```

---

# 242. Serving Runtime Testing

Serving requires:

```text
functional

numerical

performance

memory

failure
```

qualification.

---

# 243. Model Load Test

Verify:

```text
download

digest

load

warmup

readiness
```

---

# 244. Cold-Start Test

Measure:

```text
artifact missing from cache
```

scenario.

---

# 245. Warm-Start Test

Measure model already in:

```text
node cache/HBM
```

---

# 246. Cache-Invalidation Test

Change:

```text
model

tokenizer

prompt
```

and verify stale prefix cache not reused.

---

# 247. KV Memory Test

Generate:

```text
short

medium

very long
```

contexts.

Validate:

```text
memory accounting

admission

no OOM
```

# 248. KV Fragmentation Soak

Repeatedly allocate/free variable-length sequences for hours.

Watch:

```text
fragmentation
```

---

# 249. Cancellation Test

Measure:

```text
cancel propagation latency
```

---

# 250. Slow Client Test

does not stall unrelated users.

---

# 251. Continuous Batching Test

Mixed:

```text
short

long
```

generations.

# 252. Prefill Interference Test

Inject huge prompts while decode streams active.

Measure:

```text
TTFT

TPOT
```

# 253. Chunked-Prefill Qualification

Sweep chunk sizes.

Measure:

```text
throughput

TTFT

inter-token latency
```

# 254. Disaggregated Prefill/Decode Test

Measure:

```text
KV transfer latency

end-to-end benefit
```

---

# 255. Prefix Cache Test

Measure:

```text
hit correctness

hit latency

tenant isolation
```

---

# 256. Speculative Decoding Test

Evaluate:

```text
acceptance rate

latency

quality

extra compute
```

---

# 257. Quantization Validation

Test:

```text
quality

numerical drift

latency

memory

throughput
```

---

# 258. Runtime Numerical Equivalence

New runtime may not produce bit-identical outputs.

Define tolerance.

---

# 259. Absolute Tolerance

```text
|x_new - x_ref| <= ε
```

---

# 260. Relative Tolerance

```text
|x_new - x_ref|
/
|x_ref|
<= ε
```

---

# 261. Layerwise Comparison

To debug numerical regression, compare:

```text
intermediate activations
```

layer by layer.

---

# 262. Precision Change Test

FP32 → BF16/FP16/FP8/INT8 may alter:

```text
outputs

stability
```

---

# 263. GPU Generation Compatibility

Run candidate on:

```text
all supported accelerator generations
```

---

# 264. Driver Compatibility Matrix

Test:

```text
GPU

driver

runtime

framework

kernel library
```

combinations.

---

# 265. Compatibility Explosion

You cannot test every possible combination.

Define:

```text
supported matrix
```

and reject unsupported combinations.

---

# 266. Golden Hardware Profiles

Maintain known-good:

```text
runtime stack
```

per accelerator class.

---

# 267. Kernel Regression Test

New fused kernel may produce:

```text
speedup
```

but incorrect edge-case output.

Test both performance and correctness.

---

# 268. Training Runtime Testing

Distributed training needs:

```text
numerics

scale

communication

checkpoint

failure
```

qualification.

---

# 269. Single-GPU Baseline

Always establish:

```text
known-correct baseline
```

before distributed comparison.

---

# 270. DDP Equivalence Test

Compare:

```text
single GPU update

multi-GPU update
```

under equivalent global batch and deterministic settings.

---

# 271. FSDP/ZeRO Equivalence Test

Sharded training should converge similarly to:

```text
reference implementation
```

within tolerance.

---

# 272. Parallelism Layout Test

Test:

```text
DP

TP

PP

hybrid
```

layouts against reference.

---

# 273. Global Batch Test

Ensure scaling GPU count does not silently alter:

```text
effective batch
```

unless intended.

---

# 274. Gradient Test

For small model:

```text
compare gradients
```

between distributed and reference path.

---

# 275. Collective Failure Test

Kill rank during:

```text
all-reduce
```

and validate bounded failure/recovery.

---

# 276. Straggler Injection

Artificially slow one rank.

Measure:

```text
step-time amplification

straggler detection
```

---

# 277. NIC Degradation Test

Throttle one node's network.

Verify:

```text
diagnostics identify rank/link
```

---

# 278. Checkpoint Correctness Test

Save.

Restore.

Continue training.

Compare trajectory with uninterrupted run.

---

# 279. Exact Resume Test

When exact determinism required:

```text
loss sequence
```

should match.

---

# 280. Statistical Resume Test

When exact bitwise resume not required:

```text
convergence

quality
```

should remain within tolerance.

---

# 281. Topology-Change Restore Test

Checkpoint under:

```text
TP=8
```

restore under:

```text
TP=4
```

if product claims support.

---

# 282. Partial Checkpoint Test

Delete shard.

Restore should:

```text
reject checkpoint
```

rather than silently continue.

---

# 283. Corrupt Checkpoint Test

Flip bytes.

Digest validation should catch.

---

# 284. Checkpoint Manifest Test

Manifest must never reference:

```text
unfinished shard
```

---

# 285. Checkpoint Performance Test

Measure:

```text
write time

restore time

training stall
```

---

# 286. Checkpoint Storm Test

Many jobs checkpoint simultaneously.

Verify storage remains within:

```text
SLO
```

or scheduler staggers load.

---

# 287. Reproducibility

Reproducibility is not binary.

Levels include:

```text
bitwise

numerical

statistical

business-equivalent
```

---

# 288. Bitwise Reproducibility

Same bits across runs.

Often difficult on GPU/distributed systems.

---

# 289. Numerical Reproducibility

Values equal within tolerance.

---

# 290. Statistical Reproducibility

Final metrics fall within expected distribution.

---

# 291. Business Reproducibility

Business outcomes remain acceptably equivalent.

---

# 292. Reproducibility Contract

Define which level matters for:

```text
debugging

regulation

science

production
```

---

# 293. Sources of Nondeterminism

```text
random seeds

GPU atomics

thread scheduling

collective ordering

data ordering

kernel choice
```

---

# 294. Seed Capture

Record:

```text
Python

NumPy

framework

data sampler
```

random seeds where relevant.

---

# 295. Environment Capture

Record:

```text
container digest

driver

GPU type

runtime versions
```

---

# 296. Data Capture

Record immutable:

```text
dataset snapshot/manifest
```

---

# 297. Config Capture

Store:

```text
hyperparameters

feature versions

optimizer

parallelism
```

---

# 298. Reproduction Test

Select historical run.

Recreate.

Compare under declared reproducibility level.

---

# 299. Reproducibility Drift

A platform upgrade may reduce ability to reproduce old runs.

Track as compatibility risk.

---

# 300. Performance Testing

Performance is a correctness property when SLO depends on it.

---

# 301. Performance Test Types

```text
Benchmark

Load

Stress

Spike

Soak

Capacity

Scalability
```

---

# 302. Microbenchmark

Measure:

```text
single kernel

single operation

single endpoint
```

---

# 303. Microbenchmark Limitation

A faster kernel may not improve:

```text
end-to-end latency
```

if another bottleneck dominates.

---

# 304. Load Test

Run expected:

```text
production demand
```

and validate SLO.

---

# 305. Stress Test

Push beyond expected capacity until:

```text
degradation/saturation
```

---

# 306. Spike Test

Sudden demand jump:

```text
1× -> 5×
```

---

# 307. Soak Test

Run sustained load for:

```text
hours/days
```

to detect:

```text
leaks

fragmentation

drift
```

---

# 308. Capacity Test

Determine:

```text
maximum sustainable load
```

under SLO.

---

# 309. Scalability Test

Measure how performance changes with:

```text
more replicas

more GPUs

more tenants
```

---

# 310. Serving Load Model

Must include distributions:

```text
prompt lengths

output lengths

concurrency

tenant mix

cache locality
```

---

# 311. Average-Only Anti-Pattern

Average prompt:

```text
2k
```

does not represent:

```text
1% at 100k
```

---

# 312. Closed-Loop Load Generator

Waits for response before new request.

Can hide overload because generator slows when service slows.

---

# 313. Open-Loop Load Generator

Sends according to:

```text
arrival process
```

independent of service response.

Better for overload realism.

---

# 314. Coordinated Omission

A famous benchmark error:

```text
slow service reduces generated load
```

making latency look better than reality.

---

# 315. Latency Histogram

Keep full:

```text
distribution
```

not only average.

---

# 316. Tail Percentiles

Track:

```text
p95

p99

p99.9
```

---

# 317. Warm vs Cold Benchmark

Measure both:

```text
warm cache

cold cache
```

---

# 318. Failure-Mode Performance

Benchmark while:

```text
one replica missing

one zone unavailable

cache disabled
```

---

# 319. Capacity Envelope

Store:

```text
safe throughput

SLO knee

saturation

memory limit
```

for each profile.

---

# 320. Regression Threshold

Example:

```text
reject release
if p99 worsens > 10%
```

for critical benchmark.

---

# 321. Statistical Performance Regression

Benchmark variance can be noisy.

Run:

```text
multiple trials

confidence intervals
```

---

# 322. Dedicated Performance Environment

Avoid noisy neighbors when detecting:

```text
small regressions
```

---

# 323. Production Shadow Benchmark

Lab performance may differ from real traffic.

Use:

```text
shadow requests
```

where safe.

---

# 324. Shadow Traffic

Duplicate production request to candidate.

Do not use response.

---

# 325. Shadow Advantages

Tests:

```text
real input distribution

real concurrency

real cache patterns
```

---

# 326. Shadow Risks

```text
double compute

side effects

privacy

data leakage
```

---

# 327. Side-Effect-Free Shadowing

Candidate must not:

```text
send email

charge account

write durable state
```

unless sandboxed.

---

# 328. Shadow Sampling

Use:

```text
1%

5%
```

rather than 100% when cost is high.

---

# 329. Shadow Comparison

Compare candidate vs production:

```text
latency

output

errors

resource usage
```

---

# 330. Canary Testing

Candidate serves:

```text
small real user share
```

---

# 331. Canary Is Both Test and Release

It generates production evidence while limiting blast radius.

---

# 332. Canary Gates

Examples:

```text
error rate

latency

quality

cost

memory
```

---

# 333. Canary Duration

Must be long enough to observe:

```text
meaningful traffic

rare failures

business cycles
```

---

# 334. Canary Population

Use representative users where possible.

---

# 335. Canary Bias

If canary receives only:

```text
internal test traffic
```

it may miss production behavior.

---

# 336. Automatic Canary Rollback

Safe when:

```text
signal is reliable

rollback is well-defined
```

---

# 337. Manual Canary Approval

Prefer for ambiguous:

```text
quality/business
```

signals.

---

# 338. A/B Testing vs Canary

Canary asks:

```text
Is this safe?
```

A/B test asks:

```text
Which variant performs better?
```

---

# 339. Do Not Confuse Safety With Experiment Success

Candidate can be:

```text
safe but worse
```

or:

```text
better but unsafe operationally
```

---

# 340. Release Qualification

A release should pass a sequence of gates.

---

# 341. Qualification Pipeline

```text
BUILD
  |
  v
STATIC CHECKS
  |
  v
UNIT TESTS
  |
  v
INTEGRATION
  |
  v
SECURITY
  |
  v
PERFORMANCE
  |
  v
COMPATIBILITY
  |
  v
CANARY
```

---

# 342. Release Evidence Bundle

Store:

```text
test results

SBOM

signatures

benchmarks

model evaluations

approvals
```

---

# 343. Qualification Artifact

Treat evidence itself as:

```text
immutable release metadata
```

---

# 344. Policy Gate

Production admission can require:

```text
qualified = true
```

with evidence digest.

---

# 345. Requalification Trigger

Changes to:

```text
model

runtime

GPU

driver

feature definition
```

may require some or all tests again.

---

# 346. Test-Impact Analysis

Not every change needs every test.

Determine affected dimensions.

---

# 347. Example

Documentation change:

```text
no GPU benchmark
```

Kernel change:

```text
full numerical + performance suite
```

---

# 348. Qualification Matrix

Rows:

```text
change type
```

Columns:

```text
required test classes
```

---

# 349. Environment Promotion

Build once.

Promote same artifact through:

```text
dev

staging

canary

prod
```

---

# 350. Rebuild-on-Promotion Anti-Pattern

If prod artifact is rebuilt:

```text
what you tested
!=
what you deployed
```

---

# 351. Artifact Identity

Use immutable:

```text
digest
```

through all stages.

---

# 352. Test Evidence Binding

Evidence should reference:

```text
exact artifact digest
```

---

# 353. Data Release Qualification

A dataset release can have:

```text
schema

quality

freshness

lineage

privacy
```

gates.

---

# 354. Feature Release Qualification

Require:

```text
PIT correctness

offline/online parity

quality

backfill validation
```

---

# 355. Model Release Qualification

Require:

```text
evaluation

robustness

runtime compatibility

latency

governance
```

---

# 356. Runtime Release Qualification

Require:

```text
numerics

GPU matrix

performance

memory

failure recovery
```

---

# 357. Infrastructure Release Qualification

Require:

```text
policy

plan review

canary

rollback

failure test
```

---

# 358. Chaos Testing

Chaos validates:

```text
system response under failure
```

---

# 359. Chaos Is Not Random Breaking

Start with hypothesis:

```text
If storage cache fails,
running inference remains available.
```

---

# 360. Chaos Scope

Progress:

```text
process

node

rack

zone

region
```

---

# 361. Fault Types

```text
process crash

network delay

packet loss

disk full

CPU pressure

memory pressure

clock skew

dependency timeout
```

---

# 362. GPU Chaos

Inject:

```text
GPU loss

NIC throttle

driver restart

ECC-like fault
```

where safe/testable.

---

# 363. Scheduler Chaos

Kill scheduler leader during:

```text
admission

reservation

preemption
```

---

# 364. Data Chaos

Inject:

```text
late events

duplicate events

missing partitions

schema drift
```

---

# 365. Model Serving Chaos

Inject:

```text
one model replica crash

cold artifact cache

KV pressure

router stale state
```

---

# 366. DR Testing

DR tests validate recovery beyond local failures.

---

# 367. Backup Restore Test

Restore:

```text
actual production-like backup
```

into isolated environment.

---

# 368. Regional Failover Test

Move real or representative traffic away from region.

---

# 369. Empty-Region Bootstrap Test

Rebuild from:

```text
IaC + backups + artifacts
```

---

# 370. Credential-Loss Test

Verify break-glass recovery path works.

---

# 371. KMS Independence Test

Can standby decrypt artifacts independently?

---

# 372. Logical-Corruption Test

Simulate destructive metadata update.

Verify:

```text
PITR
```

restores safe state.

---

# 373. Failback Test

Recovery test is incomplete without:

```text
return path
```

---

# 374. Disaster-Capacity Test

Fail one region.

Verify survivors meet:

```text
defined degraded/full SLO
```

---

# 375. Recovery-Time Measurement

Measure actual:

```text
RTO
```

from failure injection to validated service recovery.

---

# 376. Recovery-Point Measurement

Measure actual:

```text
RPO
```

from latest surviving state.

---

# 377. Chaos Abort Condition

Every experiment needs:

```text
blast radius

automatic stop threshold
```

---

# 378. Game Day

Human + technical rehearsal of:

```text
incident response

runbooks

recovery
```

---

# 379. Testing the Humans

DR depends on:

```text
people knowing what to do
```

Game days validate that too.

---

# 380. Test Data Governance

Testing can accidentally expose:

```text
production PII
```

---

# 381. Synthetic Data

Generate realistic:

```text
structure

distribution

edge cases
```

without copying sensitive records.

---

# 382. Synthetic Data Limitation

May fail to reproduce:

```text
rare real-world complexity
```

---

# 383. De-Identified Production Data

Can offer better realism but requires strong governance.

---

# 384. Test Dataset Classification

Label:

```text
public

synthetic

internal

sensitive
```

---

# 385. Test Data Retention

Ephemeral test environments should not accumulate:

```text
sensitive copies
```

forever.

---

# 386. Production Traffic Replay

Requests may contain:

```text
PII

secrets
```

Need sanitization before replay.

---

# 387. Replay Semantics

Remove side effects.

Preserve:

```text
shape

timing

distribution
```

where possible.

---

# 388. Test Isolation

One test should not interfere with:

```text
another test

production

shared quotas
```

---

# 389. Unique Test Namespace

Use:

```text
run ID
```

for resources.

---

# 390. Cleanup Testing

Test suite should prove its own:

```text
resource cleanup
```

or ephemeral testing can become expensive.

---

# 391. Cleanup Failure

A failed E2E test can leave:

```text
100 GPUs allocated
```

Cost controls matter even in testing.

---

# 392. Test Quotas

CI/test environments should have:

```text
hard resource limits
```

---

# 393. Test Cost Attribution

Large GPU qualification can be expensive.

Track:

```text
cost per test suite

cost per release
```

---

# 394. Test Selection

Run:

```text
fast suite per commit

expensive suite nightly

full qualification before production
```

---

# 395. Test Parallelization

Independent tests can run concurrently.

But shared external state can create:

```text
flakiness
```

---

# 396. Flaky Test

A test that passes/fails without meaningful product change.

---

# 397. Flakiness Is Reliability Debt

Teams stop trusting suite.

---

# 398. Flaky-Test Budget

Track:

```text
flake rate
```

per suite.

---

# 399. Quarantine

Temporarily remove known flaky test from blocking path.

But:

```text
quarantine must have owner + deadline
```

---

# 400. Retry-on-Failure Anti-Pattern

Blindly retrying tests until green can hide real races.

---

# 401. Retry as Diagnostic

If retry passes:

```text
investigate nondeterminism
```

not simply declare success.

---

# 402. Deterministic Test Infrastructure

Control:

```text
time

randomness

external dependencies
```

where possible.

---

# 403. Flake Source Categories

```text
race

timing

shared state

external dependency

resource shortage
```

---

# 404. CI Reliability

CI itself needs:

```text
availability

capacity

observability
```

---

# 405. CI Queueing

A 2-hour test queue slows engineering velocity.

Capacity-plan CI.

---

# 406. CI Isolation

Untrusted PR should not obtain:

```text
production credentials
```

---

# 407. Ephemeral Credentials

CI receives:

```text
short-lived scoped identity
```

---

# 408. Secret Leakage Test

Scan build logs/artifacts for accidental credentials.

---

# 409. Hermetic Build

Build should not depend on uncontrolled:

```text
internet state

latest package
```

---

# 410. Reproducible Build

Same inputs should produce equivalent artifact.

---

# 411. Build Provenance

Record:

```text
source commit

builder

dependencies

parameters
```

---

# 412. Test Provenance

Record:

```text
which suite

which environment

which data

which hardware
```

produced qualification result.

---

# 413. Test Result Retention

Keep enough history for:

```text
audits

regression analysis

incident investigation
```

---

# 414. Trend Analysis

A benchmark can degrade:

```text
1% per release
```

without any single release breaching threshold.

Track trends.

---

# 415. Performance Creep

Ten releases × 3% regression can become:

```text
large cumulative loss
```

---

# 416. Quality Creep

Similarly:

```text
small slice regressions
```

can accumulate.

---

# 417. Baseline Management

Choose baseline:

```text
current production

previous release

golden implementation
```

depending on test.

---

# 418. Moving Baseline Risk

If every candidate compares only against immediately previous degraded version:

```text
slow decay goes unnoticed
```

Keep long-term golden baseline too.

---

# 419. Model Drift vs Software Regression

Test pipeline must distinguish:

```text
real-world data changed
```

from:

```text
release broke behavior
```

---

# 420. Historical Replay

Run candidate against:

```text
previous production traffic/data
```

to isolate release changes.

---

# 421. Backtesting

For time-dependent models, evaluate candidate over:

```text
multiple historical periods
```

---

# 422. Temporal Holdout

Avoid random split when:

```text
future leakage
```

would make evaluation optimistic.

---

# 423. Leakage in Evaluation

A test can be wrong even when model is correct.

Evaluation architecture itself needs validation.

---

# 424. Evaluation Dataset Governance

Track:

```text
ownership

version

lineage

contamination risk
```

---

# 425. Benchmark Contamination

LLM may have seen benchmark in training.

Use:

```text
fresh/private evaluations
```

for stronger confidence.

---

# 426. Hidden Test Sets

Can reduce optimization toward known test cases.

---

# 427. Human Evaluation

Needed when automatic metrics poorly capture quality.

---

# 428. Human Evaluation Reliability

Measure:

```text
annotator agreement

rubric consistency
```

---

# 429. Evaluation Calibration

Periodically compare automated judge against:

```text
human judgment
```

---

# 430. Model-as-Judge Testing

Judge model itself can:

```text
drift

bias

prefer verbosity
```

Validate it.

---

# 431. Evaluation Pipeline as Production System

It needs:

```text
versioning

reproducibility

monitoring
```

---

```text
  |
  v

  |
  v

  |
  v
```

# 433. Qualification Failure

```text
reason

evidence

owner

waiver path
```

---

# 434. Waiver

Sometimes release proceeds despite failed/nonexecuted test.

Must record:

```text
risk

approval

expiration
```

---

# 435. Waiver Abuse

If every release has:

```text
"temporary exception"
```

qualification system has no authority.

---

# 436. Risk-Based Testing

High-risk change:

```text
more qualification
```

Low-risk change:

```text
faster path
```

---

# 437. Change Dimensions

Risk may depend on:

```text
blast radius

state mutation

rollback difficulty

novelty

traffic share
```

---

# 438. Blast-Radius Score

Global routing change:

```text
high
```

Single internal notebook UI:

```text
low
```

---

# 439. Statefulness Score

Changing:

```text
database schema
```

is riskier than stateless frontend change.

---

# 440. Rollback Difficulty Score

Irreversible migration requires:

```text
stronger testing
```

---

# 441. Novelty Score

First deployment of new GPU runtime:

```text
higher uncertainty
```

---

```text
risk
  |
  +--> test depth
  +--> canary duration
  +--> approval level
```

```text
future qualification
```

# 490. Google-Style System Design Exercise

> Design the verification and release-qualification architecture for a global ML platform serving 10,000 engineers, 500 clusters, 100,000 model versions, millions of feature updates per second, distributed GPU training, LLM serving, RAG, agents, and five regions.

Cover:

```text
unit tests

property tests

contracts

distributed-state tests

data tests

model evaluation

GPU compatibility

performance

shadowing

canaries

chaos

DR

release qualification
```

---

# 491. Step 1 — Identify Critical Invariants

Examples:

```text
no double GPU ownership

no production pointer to missing artifact

no future leakage

no unfenced region owner
```

---

# 492. Step 2 — Map Each Invariant to Cheapest Verification Layer

Example:

```text
quota arithmetic
-> unit/property test

split-brain ownership
-> distributed fault test/formal model

regional failover
-> DR drill
```

---

# 493. Step 3 — Create Shared Test Frameworks

Provide:

```text
fake clock

fault injection

ephemeral DB

event harness

cluster simulator
```

---

# 494. Step 4 — Build Contract Registry

Track versions for:

```text
APIs

events

datasets

models

features
```

---

# 495. Step 5 — Build Data Qualification

Every dataset release receives:

```text
schema

quality

freshness

temporal

lineage
```

checks.

---

# 496. Step 6 — Build Model Evaluation Platform

Support:

```text
golden sets

holdouts

slice analysis

robustness

LLM evals
```

---

# 497. Step 7 — Build Runtime Qualification Matrix

Test every supported:

```text
GPU

driver

runtime

precision
```

profile.

---

# 498. Step 8 — Build Distributed Fault Harness

Inject:

```text
crashes

duplicates

delays

partitions

stale leases
```

---

# 499. Step 9 — Build Performance Labs

Maintain controlled:

```text
GPU

network

storage
```

environments.

---

# 500. Step 10 — Build Realistic Load Models

Use distributions from:

```text
production telemetry
```

without exposing sensitive payloads.

---

# 501. Step 11 — Add Shadow Qualification

Sample real requests to candidate systems.

---

# 502. Step 12 — Add Canary Gates

Production rollout progresses only while:

```text
safety + quality + performance
```

remain healthy.

---

# 503. Step 13 — Build DR Qualification

Automate:

```text
backup restore

regional failover

failback

empty-region bootstrap
```

tests.

---

# 504. Step 14 — Store Immutable Evidence

Bind evidence to:

```text
artifact digest
```

---

# 505. Step 15 — Enforce Production Eligibility

Admission validates:

```text
signed qualified artifact
```

for protected environments.

---

# 506. Step 16 — Add Test Impact Analysis

Select expensive tests based on:

```text
changed components

risk class
```

---

# 507. Step 17 — Feed Production Failures Back

Every serious incident should create:

```text
new regression test

new invariant monitor

or new failure drill
```

---

# 508. Step 18 — Track Test-System Health

Measure:

```text
flake rate

queue time

coverage gaps

qualification latency

cost
```

# 509. Failure Walkthrough — Quota Race Escapes Unit Tests

1. Unit arithmetic is correct.

2. Two API instances read same quota simultaneously.

3. Both reserve remaining capacity.

4. Hard quota violated.

Correct improvement:

```text
concurrent integration test

serializable/CAS invariant test
```

---

# 510. Failure Walkthrough — Feature Leakage

1. Offline AUC improves dramatically.

2. Model deployed.

3. Production quality poor.

4. Investigation finds feature used data available 2 hours after prediction time.

Permanent fix:

```text
availability-time PIT test

golden temporal dataset
```

---

# 511. Failure Walkthrough — Runtime Upgrade

1. New GPU runtime is 15% faster.

2. Canary shows rare NaNs on long sequences.

3. Release blocked.

4. Layerwise comparison finds fused attention edge-case bug.

This demonstrates:

```text
performance without numerical validation
is unsafe
```

---

# 512. Failure Walkthrough — Checkpoint Appears Valid

1. All checkpoint files exist.

2. Restore fails because one shard was incomplete.

3. Old implementation considered file existence as commit.

Fix:

```text
atomic manifest

digest validation

partial-checkpoint tests
```

---

# 513. Failure Walkthrough — Benchmark Lies

1. Closed-loop load test shows p99 = 100 ms.

2. Production spike causes p99 = 3 s.

3. Generator slowed when server slowed.

Root issue:

```text
coordinated omission
```

Fix with:

```text
open-loop arrival testing
```

---

# 514. Failure Walkthrough — Canary Misses Traffic Class

1. Internal users receive canary.

2. All tests pass.

3. External customers use much larger prompts.

4. KV OOM occurs at full rollout.

Fix:

```text
representative canary sampling

size-distribution qualification
```

---

# 515. Failure Walkthrough — Multi-Region Split Brain

1. Network partition occurs.

2. Both regions promote themselves.

3. Production pointer diverges.

A unit test cannot catch the full issue.

Required:

```text
formal ownership invariant

partition test

fencing validation
```

---

# 516. Failure Walkthrough — Evaluation Overfitting

1. Prompt tuned repeatedly against known golden set.

2. Score becomes excellent.

3. Hidden production cases degrade.

Fix:

```text
holdout suite

fresh evaluation

benchmark rotation
```

---

# 517. Failure Walkthrough — CI Becomes Bottleneck

1. Full GPU qualification runs on every commit.

2. Queue grows to 6 hours.

3. Engineers bypass tests.

Fix:

```text
risk-based test selection

fast PR suite

nightly GPU suite

release qualification
```

---

# 518. Failure Walkthrough — Flaky Test Normalization

1. Important concurrency test flakes 5%.

2. Team configures five automatic retries.

3. Race remains hidden for months.

4. Same race reaches production.

Fix:

```text
flake ownership

deterministic fault harness

no blind retries
```

---

# 519. Failure Walkthrough — DR Backup Works but Restore Does Not

1. Backup job green for a year.

2. Region fails.

3. Restore discovers missing KMS permission.

Fix:

```text
periodic end-to-end restore drills
```

---

# 526. Principal Architect Thought Process

When someone says:

> We have 90% test coverage.

```text

Code lines?

State transitions?

Failure modes?

Data contracts?

Critical user journeys?
```

# 527. Another Thought Process

When someone says:

> The controller is idempotent.

Ask:

```text

after the external side effect
```

```text
timeout with unknown outcome?
```

> The model has better offline accuracy.


# 531. Another Thought Process

When someone says:

> New inference runtime is 20% faster.

Ask:

```text
What about numerical equivalence?

HBM?

long prompts?

rare shapes?

driver matrix?
```

---

# 532. Another Thought Process

When someone says:

> Staging passed.

```text
Were caches cold?

Was one dependency missing?

Was scale representative?
```

---

# 533. Another Thought Process

When someone says:

```text
How long?

Which quality metrics?

```

```text
is the retry hiding?
```
